title: AI Tools That Are Not for Developers
description: Eleven Show HN launches aimed at everyone else: meeting capture, watch recorders, a watermark-free video editor, media generators, a tutor and a post office.
content:
# AI Tools That Are Not for Developers

The developer launches dominate Show HN, but this week a solid batch went at ordinary work: meetings you have to remember, recordings you already paid for, videos you need to cut, and letters that still have to go in the post. None of these need a terminal, and several of them exist specifically to replace something expensive.

## Meetings that stay on your machine

[[link:/tools/2049|MeetCap]] records any meeting, free, for as long as you like, and transcribes on your computer so nothing is uploaded. The useful part is not the transcript, it is the timing: if your mind drifts or the topic is new, live summaries catch you up and explain the terms, and when the meeting ends the minutes are already written - an executive summary, a recap with timestamps, speakers, to-dos with owners and due dates, and the full transcript. It also hands the whole thing to your AI agent, which can record, search past meetings or use them as context. It is macOS 14.2 and later for now.

[[link:/tools/2096|Recly]] goes at the hardware side of the same problem. A dedicated AI recorder costs around 159 dollars plus a plan once the free minutes run out, and Recly's argument is that you already own two of the three parts: the watch on your wrist and the AI you pay for. One shortcut on a Galaxy Watch or Apple Watch starts recording, transcription is free on a supported device, the original audio stays in your own Google Drive, and a ChatGPT agent starts on the minutes by itself through MCP the moment the transcript lands. It is free and open source under AGPL-3.0.

[[link:/tools/2051|Pasteface]] is the terminal-shaped version: it records, transcribes and copies speech so a dictation session goes straight to your clipboard. Recordings go into named transcript tabs, and you can keep recording while earlier chunks transcribe. It runs whisper.cpp locally or the OpenAI transcription API, depending on whether you want audio to leave the machine. Linux and macOS only.

## Editing and generating video

[[link:/tools/2065|Mastershot]] Studio is a free online video editor with no watermark on anything you export, which is the feature most free editors quietly withhold. You trim, combine and add music, text and subtitles in one project, files open straight from your computer so even a 2 GB video is ready immediately, and export gives you an MP4 up to 4K rendered on your own machine.

[[link:/tools/2091|Genjutsu AI]] does the thing text-to-video still struggles with: keep the subject and the timing, change everything around them. You add a reference video of 4 to 30 seconds and it transfers the original motion and timing into a new scene, style or set of objects, without swapping who or what is in the shot. Object swap takes up to 8 reference images for products, clothes or scenes, output goes to 1080p, and a template library lets you start from a proven setup instead of a blank prompt.

[[link:/tools/2088|Azurade]] is the plumbing behind that kind of work: one API key for Veo 3.1, Seedance and Nano Banana, covering 45 image and video models, reachable either from a REST API or from an MCP server that Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and Codex connect to with one sign-in. The billing model is the point - a credit costs between two and four cents with no subscription, credits never expire, and failed generations are refunded to the balance automatically rather than through a support ticket.

[[link:/tools/2070|Kenerate]] puts image, video and music in one workspace so you are not running three subscriptions. You start from text or reference media, choose a model, and the credit cost is shown before you generate, with free signup credits to try it.

## Learning, and running a small business

[[link:/tools/2068|Tutor]] is a self-hosted AI tutor that turns your books, online documentation and YouTube videos into an actual course rather than a chat window. You create a subject and add material - EPUB and tagged PDF files, online books and documentation by address, or YouTube videos and playlists where a video model writes the transcript including code on screen. Each source becomes a book with chapters, all of them land on one concept map, and the tutor finds the concepts, checks which you already know, then teaches the rest one at a time with numbered references back to the source and a test for each. It runs on your computer with your own key from Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or Google.

[[link:/tools/2063|Organ]] runs AI agents as departments for small agencies on a schedule. A daily pipeline clones the repository, analyses the codebase, implements changes, runs validation, reviews and opens a pull request; a content queue produces drafts with word counts; a weekly strategy review updates goals and files decisions for your review; and daily operations reports what needs you, including AI spend against a cap. Every gate is yours - merges, outbound email and publishing wait for approval unless you turn auto-publish on.

## Two that touch the physical world

[[link:/tools/2083|Zetteldesk]] is the most unexpected launch of the week: a mail agent plugin that turns a chat into a posted letter. Your agent writes the letter in Claude or ChatGPT, checks the PDF against DIN 5008, and Zetteldesk prints it, puts it in an envelope and takes it to the post office, with registered mail and proof of delivery if you want it. Before anything costs money the agent checks A4 format, the address field and page count and shows you an exact quote. It is prepaid from about 1.12 euro per letter with no subscription, works with any client supporting remote MCP servers with OAuth sign-in, and posts from Germany.

[[link:/tools/2089|SEO Audit Console]] is a free open-source MCP server that does the other offline-world job: a technical SEO audit. It pulls your crawl and Google Search Console data into a database on your own PC, merges DataForSEO and Majestic SEO into one prioritised audit, and Claude runs the analysis from there. The published walkthrough runs it on a real site with no Semrush and no Screaming Frog, and covers how findings become ranked fixes with a dashboard.

## What is actually new here

The pattern is substitution. Recly replaces a 159 dollar device, Mastershot replaces a subscription and a watermark, Azurade replaces ten vendor accounts, SEO Audit Console replaces two enterprise tools, and Zetteldesk replaces an afternoon at the post office. The AI part is almost incidental - what these launches sell is the removal of a toll.
tldr: Not every launch this week was infrastructure. MeetCap and Recly capture meetings and turn them into minutes without uploading audio, Pasteface does dictation in the terminal, Mastershot edits video in the browser with no watermark, Kenerate, Genjutsu AI and Azurade generate media, Tutor turns books and videos into a course, Organ runs agency departments, Zetteldesk posts letters an agent wrote, and SEO Audit Console runs a technical SEO audit from your own machine.
